rule_fitting_paths: Written 2026-11-22 22:57 before the run fit0-1.json (fit_ab.py, 3 rounds, held to the P-cores):
[stamp corrected 2026-11-22 23:45 to the file's creation time; the order of rule and run is as the creation times show]
one build, prev-a08daf6 (= TANG-LAB-WHU/omniMD#45). Settings of the evaluator:
def   the default (float32 at these sizes: grouped cuBLAS products; float64: the fused kernel)
per   --grouped-fitting off   (cuBLAS a net at a time)
fus   --fused-fitting 1000000 (the fused kernel for every pass; float32 first layer in tiles)
cub   --fused-fitting 0       (cuBLAS for every pass: in float64 grouped products; in float32 the default)
def2  the default again, the control
Cases: w12288, w98304 (water se_e2_a, float32, tables looked up), w12288-f64, w98304-f64 (float64, tables stored).
Measures: the fitting stage (median of the profile's device time) and the evaluation (median of the bench loop);
spread = |def2/def - 1| of the same case and measure.
1. A setting is a candidate for the default at these sizes if, in a precision, it beats def on both the fitting
stage and the evaluation by more than max(spread, 1%) at both 12,288 and 98,304 atoms.
2. If there is a candidate, PR C begins with the threshold that chooses the path (no kernel code), with the
crossover measured between the sizes the thresholds were set on (up to 4,608 rows) and these; the small
frames keep their path and serve as the control.
3. If there is none, the fitting stage is split per launch next (products and other launches, against a
standalone gemm of the same shape), and the neighbors stage into host packing, upload and kernel.

fitting_paths.what:
fit_ab.py OUT.json ROUNDS CASES LABEL=EXE[#ARG ARG ...] ...: builds and evaluator flags alternated on large frames.

CASES, joined by ',': w<atoms>[-f64][-nt] (water se_e2_a, float32 with tables unless -f64 / -nt: no tables).
Every round runs every setting on every case, in order and reversed every other round, each run
`--bench K --profile` with the extra flags of the setting after '#'. Records per run the bench loop's time and the
whole profile (device stages, host issue times, host_prepare, host_finish, wall, chunks). The card is checked for
other users before every round (tools/ht/gpu_busy.ps1). Run it held to the P-cores (tools/pk/affine.py 0xFFFC).

rule_pr_c: Written 2026-11-22 22:59, before the per-launch split of the fitting stage (nsys) and the split of the neighbors
[stamp corrected 2026-11-22 23:45 to the file's creation time; the order of rule and run is as the creation times show]
stage, which it judges. Base: prev-a08daf6. Water se_e2_a, float32 with tables looked up, 98,304 atoms (two
chunks), and 12,288 atoms as the second size.
Saving to be had, at 98,304 atoms, in ms of the evaluation:
- fitting: the stage minus what its launches would take at their ceilings: each cuBLAS product at the throughput
of the fastest kernel of the same shape seen in the traces (grouped, a net at a time or the fused path), the
other launches at the time they take now unless they are more than a fifth of the stage (then at the time their
- the search input on the host: its issue time (`issue.neighbors`) minus 0.1 ms (what a device-side packing and
upload of the positions would leave, an estimate);
- host_prepare and host_finish: not a candidate of PR C unless one of them alone is more than 1 ms.
1. PR C takes the larger of the two savings if it is at least 0.8 ms (4% of 20 ms) and at least 4% at 12,288
atoms as well; if both are, the larger at 98,304; if neither is, PR C takes the smaller follow-ups of #45 (16
lanes for the float32 exact nets, then the 968-center way) and the large frames wait for a new idea.
2. Whatever it takes is confined to large passes (rows or atoms past a threshold measured on the way), so that
the small HAP frames and committees keep their code and serve as the control of the A/B.
3. No TF32 or other tensor-core math modes for float32 (they change results): out of scope without the user.

Build prev-a08daf6 (= TANG-LAB-WHU/omniMD#45), RTX 4090, water se_e2_a.
1. rule-fit0.txt (fit0-1.json, 3 rounds alternated, held to the P-cores, card free before every round):
no candidate. Medians against def, spread from def2:
- float32 per (a net at a time): fitting +12.4% / +12.6% at 12,288 / 98,304, evaluation +0.8% / +3.4%.
- float32 fus (fused kernel for every pass): fitting +763% / +678%.
- float32 cub (cuBLAS for every pass, the default at these sizes): fitting -2.2% / +1.5%, evaluation -2.8% /
-0.1%; at 12,288 the control def2 itself was -0.8% / -3.0%, so -2.8% is not beyond the spread.
- float64 per, fus: within 0.2% of def (def is the fused kernel); cub: fitting +4.4% / +6.0%, evaluation
2. Per launch (nsys 2024.6.2, --trace=cuda, 5 evaluations a run, the last 4 compared; a kernel's
least time over them taken, as in every evaluation about three kernels took 0.35 to 0.6 ms longer than in
the others, apparently another context on the card, which drives the display). trace_min.py, fit_ceiling.py.
98,304 atoms, float32, tables looked up, kernels at their least 16.21 ms of a 20.5 to 21.1 ms window:
products of the fitting 5.28, forces 3.60, neighbor_search 2.69, descriptor 2.16, other launches of the
fitting 1.53, environment 0.78, frame sums 0.16. From the copy back of an evaluation to the first kernel of
the next the card idles about 3.2 ms (host_finish, host_prepare, the packing of the search input, then its
upload of 5.52 MB in 0.25 ms).
12,288 atoms: kernels 2.03 ms of a 2.66 to 3.43 ms window; products 0.72, forces 0.48, neighbor_search 0.36,
descriptor 0.28, other launches of the fitting 0.08, environment 0.10; the idle gap before the first
kernel 0.43 to 0.79 ms under nsys.
The grouped products are cutlass_80_simt_sgemm_grouped_128x128_8x4_align1 throughout; a net at a time cuBLAS
takes cutlass_80_simt_sgemm_256x128_8x4_nn_align1 for the first layer and ampere_sgemm_128x64_nn/_tn (or
32x128 at 12,288) for the others.
3. rule-pr-c.txt:
- fitting: products at the faster of grouped and a net at a time, layer by layer and chunk by chunk (the
fused path is far slower): 5,277 -> 4,443 us at 98,304 (saving 834 us; grouped faster only for the first
forward product of the two-net chunk), 716 -> 651 us at 12,288 (saving 65 us, 2.5% of 2.61 ms). The other
launches take 1,526 us at 98,304 against 1,783 us for their bytes at 900 GB/s (17 passes over rows x 240
entries) and 80 against 223 at 12,288 (in L2): no saving.
- search input on the host: issue.neighbors 1.555 ms at 98,304 (saving 1.455 ms) and 0.197 ms at 12,288
(saving 0.097 ms, 3.7% of 2.613 ms, 3.8% of the control's 2.536).
- host_prepare 0.66 / host_finish 0.90 ms at 98,304: neither alone above 1 ms, not a candidate.
Neither saving is at least 4% at 12,288 atoms: by rule 1, PR C takes the smaller follow-ups of #45 (16 lanes
for the float32 exact nets, then the 968-center way), and the large frames wait for a new idea.
4. Not judged by the rules, seen on the way (for the next idea, to be measured under a rule of its own):
- neighbor_search, the device kernel, is the largest launch not yet examined: 2.69 ms at 98,304 (13% of the
evaluation), 0.36 ms at 12,288 (14%). It writes index, delta and dist of every slot (about 36 bytes a slot,
